# @aponiajs/devtools

> The opt-in devtools surface for a running AponiaJS application. A disabled registration mounts nothing; an enabled one mounts an Elysia plugin that runs at `onStart`, after every route has mounted, and serves a loopback HTTP API.

The package is a leaf: nothing in the framework depends on it. An application imports `DevtoolsModule.register({ enabled })` and decides for itself whether the devtools mount at all — the framework never reads an environment variable on the application's behalf.

## What this package exports

- [DevtoolsModule](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/module/devtools-module.ts): `register(options)` builds the module an application imports; a disabled registration is inert.
- [DevtoolsOptions](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/module/devtools-module.types.ts): the required `enabled` switch, the optional loopback `port`, and the optional `logger` whose lines `/logs` records.
- [startDevtoolsServer](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/server/devtools-server.ts): starts the loopback server for one boot, or answers `undefined` when the port is taken.
- [routeRequest](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/server/request-router.ts): the pure dispatcher every request goes through.
- [AponiaMetaPayload](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/endpoints/payloads.types.ts): the `GET /__devtools/meta` payload, including the `contract` version a client checks first.
- [AponiaGraphPayload](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/endpoints/payloads.types.ts): the `GET /__devtools/graph` payload, the compiled module graph with no `routes` key.
- [AponiaRoutesPayload](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/endpoints/payloads.types.ts): the `GET /__devtools/routes` payload, every route the application answers with the binding that serves it.
- [AponiaFlowPayload](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/endpoints/flow.types.ts): the `GET /__devtools/flow` payload, the stages each mounted route passes through and the filters that answer when it throws.
- [createLogBuffer](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/logging/log-buffer.ts): the bounded log stream `/logs` publishes, and the capacity it retains.
- [tapLogBuffer](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/logging/log-tap.ts): records everything a `LoggerService` writes into a buffer, patching the logger in place.
- [AponiaLogsPayload](https://github.com/aponiajs/aponiajs/blob/release/alpha/packages/devtools/src/endpoints/payloads.types.ts): the `GET /__devtools/logs` payload, the entries after one cursor and the cursor to poll from next.

## Behavior a consumer can rely on

- A disabled module registers no provider, mounts no plugin, and opens no socket.
- An enabled module registers an `ElysiaPluginModule`, so its plugin runs at `onStart` — after every route has mounted.
- `onStart` fires on `listen()`. An application that only calls `handle()` publishes nothing and is unaffected.
- The bind address is `127.0.0.1` and is not configurable.
- A port that is already bound is reported under `Devtools` and never fails the boot: the application answers its own routes without the devtools server.
- The devtools socket stops when the application is closed, so a restart binds a fresh one.
- `GET /__devtools/meta` reports the contract version, the release that booted the application, the Elysia installed in the application's own tree (`null` when there is none), and which release supplied each artifact the boot adopted (`null` for one it did not).
- `GET /__devtools/graph` reports the graph the application compiled: its modules with their imports, controllers, providers, dependencies and exports, and its WebSocket gateways with their events. It describes the descriptor artifact's graph when the boot adopted one and the lowered decorated classes otherwise, and it carries no routes.
- `GET /__devtools/routes` reports the routes the application answers, read from the mounted table when the request arrives, so a route mounted after the boot appears too. Each route carries the method and path the table states, the module, controller and handler the boot recorded, the context fields its handler binds, and `source`: `"generated"` for a build-time invoker, `"compiled"` for the running platform's own binding, or `null` when no boot recorded the route. A route no record describes reports empty names rather than guessed ones.
- `GET /__devtools/flow` reports the stages each mounted route passes through and the filters that answer when it throws, read from the mounted table when the request arrives. The stages a route's hooks and schema state come from that table; the stages its guards and interceptors state come from the compiled plan, because the platform lowered them into one `beforeHandle` and one `afterHandle` where their order is no longer legible, so each names the class it runs. A compiled hook is published as its parts and never as a hook stage, and a contributed hook is identified by the checksum Elysia stamps rather than by a plugin name the route does not carry. Filters are a list beside the stages, never a stage in the chain.
- `GET /__devtools/logs?since=<cursor>` reports what the application logged: the registration patches the logger the application passes as `logger` and records every line into a bounded buffer from the moment the module registers, so the lines a boot writes about itself are included. An answer carries `{ cursor, entries }` with each entry shaped `{ level, context, message, timestamp }`. A cursor older than the retained window answers what is retained and one ahead of every write answers nothing, so a poll is never an error, and the cursor never goes backwards. `logger: false` publishes the stream empty, and a registration that named no logger serves no `/logs` at all.
- Every endpoint is a `GET`. Any other method answers `405` before the path is read, and a path the server does not serve answers `404`.
